title: Property Coordinator
description:
Job Description

At Crofts Estate Agents, part of the Connells Group, we're looking for a highly motivated Property Coordinator to complement our fantastic team in Cleethorpes. As our Property Coordinator you will provide property management and tenancy administration support services to branches, landlords and tenants.

What's in it for you as our Property Coordinator?
- Support in training towards ARLA - NFOPP qualifications
- Industry leading training and development
- Demonstrable career ladder
- Opportunities for progression
- Collaborative, rewarding and fun environment
- Team incentives

Key responsibilities of a Property Coordinator
- Arrange all required safety inspections and certification in line with current legislation.
- Ensure routine and additional property visits and checks are carried out in the required time frame.
- Liaise with contractors/outsourcing resources to ensure repair/maintenance works are carried out to a satisfactory standard and timescale, and in line with guarantees/warranties.
- Where possible and financially viable for the client, to claim for repair/maintenance work under insurance.
- Establish whether liability for work is landlord's or tenant's.
- Ensure that the relevant payments are instructed promptly and properly regarding contractors, deposits and landlord bills.

Skills and experience required to be a successful Property Coordinator
- Outstanding Customer Service skills
- Solid administration skills
- Resilient, positive, numerate and detail oriented
- Organised and able to prioritise workload in a fast paced environment
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills
- IT literate (MS Office, internet, email systems)

Connells Group UK is an equal opportunities employer and positively encourages applications from suitably qualified and eligible candidates regardless of , race, disability, age, sexual orientation, transgender status, religion or belief, marital status, or pregnancy and maternity.

Don't meet every single requirement? Studies have shown that women and people of colour are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. At Connells Group we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace. So, if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't fit perfectly with every aspect of the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other opportunities.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Finance Assistant to work within the Lincolnshire Police Force

Location: Nettleham, Lincoln
Contract Type: Temporary
Working Pattern: Full Time, 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Hourly Rate: £12.83 per hour
End Date: October 2027

Our client is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Exchequer Assistant to join their Finance team. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the efficient management of financial transactions within the public sector. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in supporting the delivery of a high-quality exchequer service across the Authority.

Key Responsibilities:

As an Exchequer Assistant, your duties will include:
- Processing creditor invoices promptly and accurately to ensure timely payments.
- Investigating and resolving complex queries related to invoices by liaising with both internal and external contacts.
- Undertaking HQ Cashier duties and processing petty cash returns, ensuring all costs are appropriately documented.
- Issuing petty cash upon request and managing any returns in compliance with established procedures.
- Carrying out supplier statement reconciliations as required.
- Processing Purchase Orders and managing purchases where applicable.
- Facilitating the setup of new suppliers, making informed decisions, and coordinating with internal and external contacts.
- Managing firearms refunds and processing Boarding Up invoices, investigating each incident accordingly.
- Booking travel and hotel accommodations and addressing any related queries.
- Resolving exchequer-related inquiries promptly and courteously.
- Ensuring all exchequer processes adhere to predetermined timelines.
- Promoting best practises in exchequer matters across the organisation, providing training and guidance to personnel as needed.

Requirements:
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in financial processing.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to work collaboratively within a team and provide exceptional support to colleagues and external partners.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and the ability to manage multiple tasks effectively.
- Familiarity with financial systems and processes is advantageous.

Why Choose This Role?

Join a dedicated Finance team committed to upholding the highest professional standards.
Be part of an organisation that values ethical conduct and diversity.
Contribute to meaningful work within the public sector, supporting the community and ensuring financial integrity.

Additional Information:

The duties outlined in this advertisement are not exhaustive. The successful candidate may be required to undertake additional responsibilities within the general scope of the role. The organisation promotes a culture of equality and diversity and is committed to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults.

If you are enthusiastic about making a difference in the finance sector and possess the skills required for this role, this could be the perfect opportunity for you!

For more information and to apply for the Exchequer Assistant position, please contact the recruitment agency today. Seize the chance to elevate your career while contributing to a vital public service!

title: Administrator
description: This is an exciting opportunity to join an established Lincolnshire Talking Therapy service as a B2 Administrative Assistant for the Skegness LTT Team. We are looking for an organised, flexible, efficient team player to join our busy mental health talking therapies service. The successful applicant will be based at Holly Lodge, Skegness, supporting service delivery, working Mon- Friday. The service will provide regular supervision and training to support this. You will require excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, as well as having an exemplary telephone manner, with the initiative to work on your own at times. Lincolnshire Talking Therapies is a successful service that provides a stepped care model for the treatment of people with mild to moderate mental health problems. For further information please contact Pamela Dennis, Team Manager, Skegness LTT via email at Pamela.dennis6@nhs.net We are not able to offer sponsorship for this role. Please provide details of the visa type and expiry date in your application. Failure to provide the required information will result in your application being rejected. As an Administrator, you will play a crucial role in supporting the smooth operation of our talking therapies service. You'll assist both clinical and non-clinical teams, ensure a welcoming environment for all visitors, and develop essential skills for a future NHS career. To undertake reception and routine administration duties in support of clinical and non-clinical activity, ensuring a professional and efficient reception service is provided for all visitors, including service users, carers, contractors, external and internal stakeholders, along with site colleagues and teams. Main Duties of the Apprentice Administrator (Mental Health NHS Talking Therapies): - Provide administrative support to the talking therapies team, including answering phones and responding to emails. - Assist with booking appointments, managing waiting lists, and scheduling assessments. - Maintain accurate and confidential patient records in line with NHS policies. - Welcome and guide service users, families, and visitors to the service. - Support the preparation and distribution of clinical documents, letters, and reports. - Help to organise meetings and take minutes when required. - Input data and generate routine reports for the team. - Work closely with clinical and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth running of the service. - Uphold patient confidentiality and treat all information sensitively. - Undertake general office tasks such as photocopying, scanning, and filling Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details regarding this position.

title: Receptionist
description: The GP receptionist is responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception duties and providing support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties may include, but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, effective use of the appointment system, booking appointments, processing of personal information and assisting patients as required. To act as a central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with the multidisciplinary team member and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The core responsibilities of the receptionist are as follows. On occasion, there may be a requirement to carry out tasks not listed below, that are within the reasonable scope of the role. Maintain and monitor practice appointment system Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments Answer incoming phone calls, dealing with the callers request appropriately Signpost patients to the correct service Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as requested Input data as necessary onto patients healthcare records Direct requests for information to relevant team members i.e., SAR, DVLA forms, insurance/solicitors letters Manage all queries as necessary in an efficient manner Carry out system searches as requested Support all clinical staff with general tasks as required Photocopy documentation as required Maintain a clean, tidy and effective working area Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards In addition to the core responsibilities, the Receptionist may be requested to; 1. Action incoming emails and correspondence as necessary 2. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the rota 3. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead 4. Support admin team, providing cover during absences 5. Scan patient related documents and attach scanned documents to patients healthcare record We currently have 2 part time vacancies available allowing us to be flexible for the right candidate. All hours will be worked between 08:00 and 18:30, Monday to Friday

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are seeking a part time Medical Receptionist to join our friendly team 17.5 hours a week. Monday 12.30pm-6.30pm, Wednesday 1pm-6.30pm and Friday 12.30pm-6.30pm. Flexibility will be required. There is also a Saturday rota which you would be required to be part of which will be a maximum of 2 Saturdays per year. Duties will involve: - answering the Practices telephone and assisting patients in a courteous, efficient and effective manner - to assist in patients prescriptions - greeting and dealing with patients and other visitors either in person or via the telephone - process personal and telephone requests to book appointments, visits and telephone consultations - taking messages and efficient communications - filing, retrieving paperwork and photocopying - processing and management of patient registrations - computer data entry/data allocation and collation - be part of a large shared rota for the occasional out of hour shift We are seeking a Medical Receptionist to join our friendly team. Duties will involve: - assist in processing repeat prescriptions - greeting and dealing with patients and other visitors either in person or via the - taking messages and passing on information - be part of a large shared rota for the occasional early evening, weekend or Bank holiday shift - end of day closure
